situation: Your new phone stopped working in a week and the shop says 'company's problem'.
say: This is cheating! I'll never come to your shop again.
better: The phone stopped working in seven days. I'd like a replacement under warranty. What's the process, and how long will it take?
also: I bought it here last week. Please raise the warranty claim for me today.
weak: Bhaiya, please, something do na, I'm a regular customer.
Okay, no problem, I'll see what to do.
why: States the facts and the exact remedy you want, calmly.

situation: Your landlord has not fixed a leaking bathroom pipe for three weeks.
say: Uncle, kindly do the needful regarding the pipe at the earliest.
better: Uncle, the bathroom pipe has leaked for three weeks and the wall is getting damp. Can a plumber come by Saturday?
also: If it's not fixed by Saturday, I'll call a plumber and deduct it from rent. Is that okay?
weak: Uncle, no hurry, whenever you get time.
Every month I pay rent and you do nothing.
why: Specific problem, impact and deadline get action; vague requests get delays.

situation: An online order arrived damaged, and the chatbot keeps looping.
say: Worst service ever!!! Pathetic company, will post on Twitter.
better: Order 4521 arrived with a cracked screen. Photos attached. I'd like a replacement or full refund within five days, please.
also: Please connect me to a human agent. The bot can't handle damaged-item claims.
weak: Hello? Anyone there? Reply fast.
Sorry to disturb, but if possible can you please check?
why: Order number, evidence and a clear request make a complaint easy to resolve.

situation: A restaurant got your order wrong for the second time.
say: Kya bakwaas hai, can't you people even write one order?
better: This isn't what I ordered. It's the second time today. Could you please replace it quickly?
also: I asked for no onion, and it has onion. I'd like it remade, please.
weak: It's okay, I'll just eat this.
Forget it, I'll eat it, but zero tip.
why: Firm and polite: the problem, then the fix you want.

situation: A friend joked about your weight in front of others, and it hurt.
say: Haha, okay, very funny.
better: That comment about my weight hurt, especially in front of everyone. Please don't joke about that again.
also: I know you didn't mean harm, but it didn't feel like a joke to me.
weak: Whatever, I don't care what you think.
No problem, I'm used to such jokes.
why: Name the exact words and how they felt; avoid sulking or attacking.

situation: Your partner forgot an important plan you had made weeks ago.
say: You never care about anything I say.
better: I felt hurt when you forgot tonight's dinner. It mattered to me. Can we talk about what happened?
also: I was really looking forward to it, so I'm disappointed.
weak: Fine, it's okay, I'm used to being last.
Every single time you do this, you're so selfish.
why: 'I felt' about one event, not 'you never', keeps the fight fair.

situation: A colleague presented your idea as his own in a meeting.
say: Wow, nice of you to steal my idea.
better: Rahul, the pricing idea you presented was the one I shared with you on Monday. Next time I'd like to present my own work.
also: I'd like to be credited for that idea. Can we clear it up with the team?
weak: Some people can only shine with others' work, na?
It's fine, ideas belong to everyone.
why: Calm facts and a clear request; no sarcasm, no gossip.

situation: You were passed over for promotion without any explanation.
say: Okay sir, as you wish. No issues.
better: I was disappointed not to get the promotion. Could you tell me what I need to show to be ready next cycle?
also: I'd like honest feedback on why I wasn't picked this time.
weak: This is pure politics, everyone knows it.
I'll start looking elsewhere, then you'll know.
why: Shows discontent honestly and turns it into a clear next step.

situation: Your manager keeps messaging you late at night with non-urgent tasks.
say: Sure sir, will do immediately.
better: I've noticed many late-night messages lately. Unless it's urgent, I'll pick them up first thing at 9.
also: Could we keep after-hours messages for real emergencies?
weak: Sir, I also have a life, you know.
Sir, don't you sleep? Even I need rest.
why: States the pattern and your plan, without accusing.

situation: A neighbour plays loud music past midnight every weekend.
say: Some people have no manners at all.
better: Hi, I'm from flat 302. The music carries into our bedroom after midnight. Could you turn it down after eleven?
also: We have a small child who wakes up. Would eleven be okay as a cut-off?
weak: Oye, turn it off! People are sleeping here!
Sorry to disturb, if possible, maybe a little lower? Only if okay.
why: Go to the person first, with the effect and a fair ask.

situation: You are angry, and you feel you might say something harsh.
say: Just leave me alone! I don't want to talk!
better: I'm too angry to talk well right now. Give me twenty minutes, then let's sort it out.
also: I need a short break so I don't say something I regret.
weak: Say whatever you want, I'm done.
I don't care anymore, do what you want.
why: Calm anger: name it, pause, and promise to come back.

situation: The cab driver demands extra money above the app fare.
say: Bhaiya, what is this loot? Are you mad?
better: The app shows 340, so I'll pay 340. If there's a problem, I'm happy to raise it with the app's support.
also: I'll pay the fare on the app, not more.
weak: Okay, okay, take it, just let me go.
Fine, but I'm giving you one star.
why: Calm, firm and backed by facts, without insults.

situation: A family member criticised your career choice at a family dinner.
say: You all never support me, you only know how to taunt.
better: It hurt to hear that in front of everyone. I've thought hard about this choice. I'd like your support, or at least your respect.
also: If you have concerns, talk to me privately, not at the dinner table.
weak: Fine, I'll leave this house then.
Haan, I'm the failure of the family, happy now?
why: Says the hurt and what you need, without a counter-attack.

situation: Your internet has been down for four days and calls to support go nowhere.
say: Sir, please, I'm requesting you, please do something.
better: My connection has been down for four days. Complaint number 7781. I want a technician by tomorrow and a credit for the lost days.
also: Please escalate this to a supervisor. I've called three times already.
weak: Your company is useless, I'm cancelling right now.
Okay, whenever possible, no problem.
why: Facts, reference number and a clear remedy push a stuck complaint forward.

situation: You feel your team lead treats one colleague's work more favourably.
say: Obviously, she's your favourite, so she gets everything.
better: I've noticed the good projects often go to the same person. Could you tell me how assignments are decided?
also: I'd like a shot at the next big project. What would I need to show?
weak: Sir, I'm also working hard, no one sees.
It doesn't matter, nobody cares here.
why: Raise the pattern as a question, not an accusation.

situation: A friend borrowed your bike and returned it scratched without saying anything.
say: Accha, so this is how you return things.
better: The bike has a new scratch on the side. Did something happen? I'd like us to share the repair cost.
also: I'm a bit upset you didn't mention it. Let's sort out the repair.
weak: Never mind, it's just a bike.
You never take care of anything, typical.
why: Names what happened and the fix, without sarcasm.

situation: You have to write a formal complaint to a hospital about rude staff.
say: Your staff is very rude and arrogant. Take strict action.
better: On 12 March, at the billing desk, a staff member shouted at my mother. I request an inquiry and a written reply.
also: I've attached the bill and time of visit for reference.
weak: Respected sir, with due respect, I humbly beg to state that staff was rude.
Your hospital is a disgrace, worst ever.
why: Date, place and what happened make a complaint credible and actionable.

situation: Your sibling read your private messages without asking.
say: You're such a cheap person, how dare you!
better: You read my messages without asking. That's a line for me. Please don't do it again.
also: I feel my privacy was broken. I need you to respect it.
weak: Fine, now I'll read yours too.
Okay, whatever, nothing is private in this house anyway.
why: States the action and the boundary, calmly, without name-calling.

situation: Your appraisal rating seems unfair compared to your work this year.
say: This rating is totally wrong. I'm very demotivated.
better: I disagree with this rating. I delivered both launches on time. Can we go through the reasons and the evidence together?
also: I'd like to understand how this was decided, and request a review.
weak: Okay, fine, as you feel.
Then why should I work hard next year?
why: Disagree with evidence and a request, not just a feeling.

situation: A friend often cancels at the last minute, and you are fed up.
say: Typical you. I knew you'd cancel.
better: This is the third time you've cancelled last minute. It's frustrating, because I plan around it. What's going on?
also: I'd rather you said no early than cancelled on the day.
weak: No worries, it's totally fine!
Forget it, I won't plan anything with you again.
why: Count the pattern, say the effect, and ask, instead of sniping.

situation: The builder has delayed your flat's possession by over a year.
say: You builders are all frauds. I'll go to the media.
better: Possession was due in March last year. I need a written new date and the delay compensation in the agreement.
also: If I don't get a reply in fifteen days, I'll approach RERA.
weak: Please sir, at least give some idea, we're suffering a lot.
Okay, we'll wait, what else can we do.
why: Cite the agreement, ask for specifics, and name a fair next step.

situation: A co-worker keeps interrupting you in meetings.
say: Excuse me, can I please speak or should I just leave?
better: Let me finish this point, then I'd like to hear your view.
also: Can I just complete this? I'm almost done.
weak: Sorry, sorry, you go ahead.
You always do this, you never let anyone talk.
why: Hold your turn calmly in the moment; no drama, no surrender.

situation: You feel taken for granted because you always host family gatherings.
say: Haan haan, I'll do it, who else will.
better: I've hosted the last five gatherings, and I'm tired. Can someone else host Diwali this year?
also: I'm happy to help, but I'd like us to take turns hosting.
weak: Nobody in this family thinks about me.
Fine, but this is the last time I'm doing anything.
why: Replace martyr sighs with a fact and a fair request.

situation: Your manager criticised you harshly in front of the team.
say: Sorry sir, my mistake, won't happen again.
better: Can we talk for a minute? I'm open to feedback, but I'd prefer criticism one to one, not in front of the team.
also: I want to fix the issue. Could we discuss it privately?
weak: Sir, you can't talk to me like that.
Fine, I'll quietly start updating my CV.
why: Accepts the feedback, but sets a respectful line on how it is given.

situation: A bank charged you a fee you never agreed to.
say: Why are you looting customers? Remove this charge now.
better: There's a 590 rupee charge on my statement that I didn't authorise. Please explain it in writing and reverse it if it's an error.
also: If it isn't resolved in seven days, I'll take it to the banking ombudsman.
weak: Okay, maybe it's some rule, I'll pay.
Please, I'm a poor customer, please help.
why: Exact amount, clear ask and a fair next step get a proper response.
